decisions.reason: As a plugin close to the core shop offer, with sunk development and listing commitments already made, management would likely keep it and explain any limited traction by niche demand or client-specific timing.
The ERP interface plugin fits the firm's stated move toward broader multichannel and tailored commerce support, so prior investment and strategic visibility strongly favor continuation.

Although one of several similar price-comparison tracking plugins, it still supports the firm's measurable marketing promise and management would tend to justify continued support rather than admit a failed launch.

Because it remains adjacent to the established optimization business and likely has reusable code and client integrations, the firm would be inclined to persist and attribute weak demand to temporary market conditions.
Its overlap with other tracking plugins makes withdrawal somewhat more plausible, but growth, ongoing R&D, and escalation of commitment still make retention more likely than immediate abandonment.
